# The complete correspondence of law and history

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> A family of histories is a law's exactly where it holds its splices, and histories fix a law up to its dead ends.

`histories-fix-law-up-to-dead-ends` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Let S be a type of configurations and A one of moves; a history is a pair of sequences g : ℕ → S and m : ℕ → A. A law P admits a history (Admits P g m) where every step the history takes is a step of P; a run's history is admitted by its law (Run.admits). The law a family of histories H shows (ShownBy H) has as steps the steps its histories take; it is the least law admitting each history of H (ShownBy.admits, shownBy_le_iff). A family holds its splices (SpliceClosed H) where every sequence made of its own steps is in it. The histories of a law hold their splices (admits_spliceClosed), and a family is the family of some law's histories exactly where it holds its splices, the law it shows being one such law (family_iff). A family is consistent (ConsistentFamily H) where no two of its histories take one move at one configuration to two outcomes; the law it shows is determined exactly then (shownBy_determined_iff), and a family is the family of a determined law's histories exactly where it holds its splices and is consistent (determined_family_iff). The live steps of a law (live P) are those some history of it takes; a law and its live steps admit the same histories (admits_live_iff), two laws admit the same histories exactly where they have the same live steps (same_histories_iff), the live law has no dead end (live_live), and the dead end's step is not live (DeadEnd.not_live). So laws up to their dead ends and families holding their splices correspond one to one: splicing and dead ends are the whole law of law and history. With histories that stop no dead end remains: two laws have the same finite histories exactly where they have the same steps (same_finite_histories_iff), and a family of finite histories is a law's exactly where it is made of its steps, the empty course going nowhere and a course being a first step followed by the rest (MadeOfSteps, finite_family_iff). The dead end is a fact of unending histories. No premise.

Canonical source: [Histories.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Histories.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- No premise: family_iff, determined_family_iff, shownBy_determined_iff, same_histories_iff and admits_live_iff are two-way and hold for every law and every family of histories.
- Histories are of two kinds: unending sequences (the core's runs) and finite courses (Trace); dead ends occur only in the first.
- A family is a predicate on pairs of sequences; families are compared by equivalence at every history, without function extensionality.

P76 (work board), following Ren's “move towards 100%” of 12 October 2026: completeness in the strong sense, the laws of a kind being all its laws, held before for counting only (tally_iff_counted). P69 proved that a history fixes the law it shows and named where the correspondence is not an identity, dead ends and splices; this shows that these two are the whole of it. Reading (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): Ren agreed that law and history are one unfolding read two ways, the law read off the unfolding (“there are no two realities”); with this result, a law read off histories is a family of histories holding its splices and nothing else; what a law set over the unfolding can add are dead ends, which no history shows; the splice is memory's absence: a law answers from where one is, not from how one came there. See the integration document §98.

The same receipt covers the package's 75 modules (including the import-only root and the bridge) with 4518 theorems/6370 declaration audits, and 22 inherited modules whose current bytes match passed receipts; periphery receipt 20261013T095049.338744Z passed. The checker also verifies core purity: the import closure of the core (GenerativeCore, InquirySufficiency, RelationalRenewal, L1–L4 and the root module Becoming) is exactly these 77 modules, every source declaration in it has an empty axiom report (of the constants Lean generates, only the injectivity lemmas of constructors with fields, injEq, depend on propext; no source declaration uses them, and the checker lists them), and it compiles from Lean's prelude alone (the foundation's import Std removed for that run). The author's counterreview is in §98 of the integration note; there is no independent review yet.

Whether an actual unfolding's histories stop is not stated; which family an actual unfolding is is not stated; the readings are the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation; no ethical predicate occurs.

- Dead end: a law with a step and no history (DeadEnd.no_history), whose step is not live (DeadEnd.not_live); splice: the law a revisiting history shows admits a history it never took (Splice.spliced).
